author: GDS Investments
title: Apple ( AAPL ) and Qualcomm ( QCOM ) will probably settle th
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) and Qualcomm ( QCOM ) will probably settle their legal dispute without either side achieving a clear victory, while EU regulators are reportedly prepared to authorize Qualcomm’s takeover of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ), and investors will benefit either from a consummation or termination of the deal. Furthermore, Broadcom ( AVGO ) will probably have to either raise its takeover bid for Qualcomm or abandon its efforts to buy the company. Given all of these positive catalysts, along with Qualcomm’s low valuation, Qualcomm stock looks well positioned to rise from current levels, and investors should buy the shares.
Regarding the litigation between Qualcomm and Apple, both sides appear to have some strong arguments. Both companies credibly allege that the other is infringing on multiple patents . Qualcomm appears to have a leg up in patent law, given its high R&D spending, Apple’s high profit margins, and the fact that consumers would probably be hurt by an Apple victory. But Apple seems to have a decent antitrust argument, in light of Qualcomm’s high market share.
Usually, when both sides have good arguments in corporate litigation, a settlement is made which doesn’t tremendously help or hurt either side. For example, Apple settled its patent litigation with Nokia, and Amazon ( AMZN ) settled a lawsuit with Broadcom. Since Qualcomm stock has missed out on the huge rallies over the last year in the chip sector, rising just 1.5% since January 2017, in large part because of investors’ fear that the chip maker would be dealt a knockout blow by Apple in court, Qualcomm stock should rally once a deal is made.
Meanwhile, the EU is reportedly set to approve Qualcomm’s takeover of NXP Semiconductors , potentially clearing the way for the acquisition to be carried out and removing another overhang on Qualcomm stock. And if the deal is blocked by regulators or NXP investors, Qualcomm has pledged to implement a “large” share buyback initiative, so Qualcomm investors are in a win-win situation on that front.
Qualcomm investors will probably reject Broadcom’s $70 per share offer, consisting of $60 in cash and $10 in Broadcom stock, or Broadcom will raise the offer. First of all, Qualcomm stock is very close to the $70 per share level, despite the Apple litigation overhang, while the stock market and world and U.S. economic growth are all looking quite strong. Additionally, $70 per share is a low price, given the company’s fiscal 2019 earnings per share guidance (see below). Meanwhile, Qualcomm’s core chip business looks poised to take off, driven by the growth of the Internet of Things in general and connected and driverless cars, where NXP Semiconductor is a major player , in particular. 

At current levels, Qualcomm still offers investors a healthy 3.35% dividend yield. And on January 16, the company provided fiscal 2019 earnings per share guidance of $6.75-$7.50. If the company generates EPS of $7, its stock is currently trading at a forward price to earnings ratio of less than 10, despite its positive growth catalysts and its high dividend yield.
Apple and Qualcomm will likely settle their litigation, while Qualcomm’s investors will either benefit from NXP’s strength in the connected/driverless car market or a large share buyback. Additionally, Broadcom’s bid is likely to either be raised or rejected, given the positive macro environment, Qualcomm’s strong fiscal 2019 EPS guidance, and the positive catalysts of its business. Finally, Qualcomm’s stock looks undervalued at current levels. In light of all these points, Qualcomm stock is quite attractive, as it has many GARP and deep value attributes.
